chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Umar ibn Aban, from Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Can I marry the woman for a month, so I withhold something from her?' He said, 'Yes, take from her by the measure of whatever she has differed. If it was half a month, then the half (dower), and if it was a third, then the third.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) – similar to it.

key_terms.تُخْلِفُكَ: she differs with you / withholds from you

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on withholding the dower if a husband does not consummate the marriage for part of the agreed period?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of proportional dower (mahr) based on the duration of conjugal rights, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding temporary or permanent marriage contracts. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the husband's obligation is strictly tied to the actual time the wife is available for intimacy, ensuring fairness if he withholds consummation. This ruling underscores the contractual nature of marital rights in Shia jurisprudence, where financial obligations are directly linked to the fulfillment of specific duties.
